title: Compatible contractive averages on finite-quotient functions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a nonarchimedean normed field $B$ containing $\mathbf Q_\ell$ isometrically [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], so $|x+y|\leq\max(|x|,|y|)$. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of open normal subgroups at the identity, and suppose every finite continuous quotient of $K$ has order prime to $\ell$. Let $C(K,B)$ be the continuous $B$-valued functions with supremum norm. For an open normal subgroup $U$, write $Q_U=K/U$ and $\pi_U:K\to Q_U$. Define $D\subseteq C(K,B)$ to consist of all $f=g\circ\pi_U$ for some open normal $U$ and some function $g:Q_U\to B$. Each $Q_U$ is finite and nonempty. The set $D$ is a $B$-linear subspace containing the constants and preserved by the translations $T_a^Lf(h)=f(ah)$ and $T_a^Rf(h)=f(ha)$ for $a\in K$. There is a well-defined $B$-linear map $A:D\to B$ such that for every such representation of $f$,
$$A(f)=|Q_U|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q_U}g(q).$$
In particular, if $V\subseteq U$ are open normal subgroups, $\rho:Q_V\to Q_U$ is the quotient map, and $g:Q_U\to B$, then
$$|Q_V|^{-1}\sum_{z\in Q_V}g(\rho(z))=|Q_U|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q_U}g(q).$$
Moreover $|A(f)|\leq\|f\|_\infty$, $A(1)=1$, and $A(T_a^Lf)=A(f)=A(T_a^Rf)$ for all $a\in K$, $f\in D$. Completeness of $B$ is not assumed. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: For an open normal subgroup $U$, the cosets $kU$ are open: translation by $k$ is a homeomorphism with inverse translation by $k^{-1}$. They cover $K$, so compactness supplies a finite subcover. Cosets are disjoint or equal (if $ku=lv$, then $kU=lU$), hence these finitely many distinct cosets are all of $Q_U$. The identity coset makes $Q_U$ nonempty. Give $Q_U$ the discrete topology; every inverse image under $\pi_U$ is a union of open cosets, so $\pi_U$ is continuous and surjective. Normality makes the product $(kU)(hU)=khU$ well defined, so this is a finite continuous quotient group and its positive order is prime to $\ell$ by hypothesis. Every $g:Q_U\to B$ is continuous since its domain is discrete; thus $g\circ\pi_U$ really lies in $C(K,B)$.

proof.text: If $U_1,U_2$ are open normal subgroups, then $W=U_1\cap U_2$ is open and normal. The maps $\rho_i:K/W\to K/U_i$, $kW\mapsto kU_i$, are well defined and surjective, and $\pi_{U_i}=\rho_i\circ\pi_W$. Consequently, if $f_i=g_i\circ\pi_{U_i}$ and $b_1,b_2\in B$, then $b_1f_1+b_2f_2=(b_1g_1\circ\rho_1+b_2g_2\circ\rho_2)\circ\pi_W$. The zero function and every constant factor through $K/K$, which is a singleton. This proves that $D$ is a $B$-linear subspace containing constants. For $a\in K$, the translated functions factor through the same $Q_U$, via $q\mapsto g(\pi_U(a)q)$ and $q\mapsto g(q\pi_U(a))$ respectively. Thus both translations preserve $D$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar auxiliary context only; elementary finite-quotient argument supplied by Q113, not asserted to occur in the blueprint. Step 2.

proof.text: Let r:X→Y be a surjective homomorphism of finite groups and g:Y→B. For each y choose a lift a∈X. Left multiplication by a permutes X, so Σ_x g(y r(x))=Σ_x g(r(x)). For each x, right multiplication by r(x) permutes Y, so Σ_y g(y r(x))=Σ_y g(y). Summing the first identity over Y, interchanging the two finite sums, and applying the second gives |Y| Σ_x g(r(x))=|X| Σ_y g(y). The embedding of the characteristic-zero field of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] makes B characteristic zero. Both group orders are positive and hence nonzero in B; dividing gives equality of normalized averages. Apply this to the canonical quotient homomorphism K/V→K/U, which is surjective because each coset has a representative in K. This double-sum argument replaces explicit fiber counting in the original plan.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar auxiliary context only; elementary finite-quotient argument supplied by Q113, not asserted to occur in the blueprint. Step 3.

proof.text: Given two representations $f=g_1\circ\pi_{U_1}=g_2\circ\pi_{U_2}$, take $W=U_1\cap U_2$ as above. Surjectivity of $\pi_W$ implies $g_1\circ\rho_1=g_2\circ\rho_2$ as functions on $Q_W$: evaluate at a lift $k$ of each $w\in Q_W$. The refinement identity of step 3 says that each proposed value of $A(f)$ equals the average of this single function on $Q_W$. Hence define $A(f)$ by any representation; its value is independent of that choice. For $f_1,f_2$ and $b_1,b_2$ use their common quotient from step 2 and distribute its finite sum to obtain $A(b_1f_1+b_2f_2)=b_1A(f_1)+b_2A(f_2)$. This constructs the required $B$-linear map with every finite-quotient formula.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar auxiliary context only; elementary finite-quotient argument supplied by Q113, not asserted to occur in the blueprint. Step 4.

proof.text: For a representation f=g∘π_U, coprimality and Padic.norm_natCast_eq_one_iff give norm one for the quotient order in Padic l. NormedAlgebra makes algebraMap isometric, so the order and its inverse also have norm one in B. Bound the norm of the finite sum by ‖f‖ directly: each g(q) equals f(k) for a representative k of q, hence has norm at most ‖f‖ by the continuous-map supremum-norm inequality. Induct over the finite summation set. The empty sum has norm zero; the ultrametric inequality bounds each added term and the previous partial sum by ‖f‖. Multiplication by the inverse group order preserves this bound. No maximum, limit, or completeness is needed; the scalar facts are those of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar auxiliary context only; elementary finite-quotient argument supplied by Q113, not asserted to occur in the blueprint. Step 5.

proof.text: For $a\in K$, the quotient maps $q\mapsto\pi_U(a)q$ and $q\mapsto q\pi_U(a)$ are permutations of $Q_U$, with inverses multiplication by $\pi_U(a)^{-1}$ on the corresponding side. Reindexing the finite sums in the representations of step 2 therefore gives $A(T_a^Lf)=A(f)=A(T_a^Rf)$. Finally $\sum_{q\in Q_U}1=n$, so $A(1)=n^{-1}n=1$. All sums and quotient sets are finite and the subspace consists of actual functions on $K$; choose the ambient universes as in [def-weil-size-convention].
